units.text: INT. WHOLESALE FLOWER MARKET - 4 A.M.
Concrete floor slick with water and petals.
Buckets of peonies, ranunculus, lilies stacked to the ceiling.
Forklifts beep somewhere in the vaulted dark.
The air smells green and cold.
AURELIO FONTANA (30s, florist, rolled sleeves, thorn scratches on his forearms) lifts a bucket of white ranunculus in each hand and sets them on his cart.
BEATRIX HALLORAN (30s, rival florist, canvas apron, sleeves tied around her waist) reaches for the same stems and comes up with his hand.
They freeze.
The bucket tips between them, spilling cold water over both their boots.
He lunges to save it and she lunges at the same instant, and they collide, and white petals burst into the air like startled birds.
Those were mine.
units.name: AURELIO

units.text: They were on the floor.
units.name: BEATRIX

units.text: In my bucket.
units.name: AURELIO

units.text: In a puddle.
units.name: BEATRIX

units.text: JUN (20s, market porter, headphones, a hand truck) rolls past, glances at them, and rolls on without comment.
Aurelio's phone buzzes in his apron.
He fishes it out and puts it to his ear.
Aurelio? Aurelio, the roses, did you get the roses?
units.name: NONNA

units.text: Nonna, it's four in the morning.
units.name: AURELIO

units.text: The wedding is at eleven. A wedding doesn't care what time it is.
units.name: NONNA

units.text: I know. I'm at the market right now.
units.name: AURELIO

units.text: Who are you with? I hear a girl.
units.name: NONNA

units.text: Beatrix covers a laugh.
Aurelio turns his shoulder, and Beatrix picks a ranunculus from the floor and tucks it behind his ear while he is distracted.
A colleague, Nonna.
units.name: AURELIO

units.text: Is she pretty?
units.name: NONNA

units.text: I'll call you back.
units.name: AURELIO

units.text: He hangs up.
He pulls the flower from his ear, studies it, doesn't give it back.
You can keep the ranunculus. But I'm taking the peonies.
units.name: BEATRIX

units.text: Fine.
units.name: AURELIO

units.text: And the lilies.
units.name: BEATRIX

units.text: Beatrix.
units.name: AURELIO

units.text: Yes?
units.name: BEATRIX

units.text: Whose wedding is it?
units.name: AURELIO

units.text: Mine, in a way. My sister's. Eleven o'clock.
units.name: BEATRIX

units.text: Ours is eleven too.
units.name: AURELIO

units.text: They look at each other.
Jun rolls past again, in the other direction, headphones still on, humming.
